$comment: D-MIR-TRY-FILTER-WITH-A-BRANCH-REFUSED: a __try FILTER whose expression has a branch. `&&`, `||` and `?:` evaluate an operand on one path only, so a filter written with any of them is more than one basic block — `__except (GetExceptionCode() == EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION && g == 1)`, and the shape the vendor's documentation writes a filter in, `cond ? EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER : EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH`. A filter is compiled as a function of its own, and the whole of its expression — every path — belongs to that function. Before the fix every such filter was REFUSED, at baseline and in release (the region's skeleton took a filter to be one block). Ten cases, each a function of its own: `&&` over a global, the conditional choosing the disposition, a logical OR whose left is false, `&&` over a local of the function, an inner filter that declines through its conditional while the outer region takes the fault, the right operand of `&&` not evaluated when the left is false and evaluated once when it holds, branches inside branches with a call that takes the exception record, a handler naming a global only its filter named, a region inside a loop, a filter that sees a store the guarded body made before it faulted. The exit code names the first case to fail (11..20); 42 = all right; a crash = a filter declined a fault it should have accepted. The reference compiler (cl 19.51 x64, /Od and /O2) runs this file to 42. The release arm is the same file through the optimizer. ON A HOST THAT IS NOT WINDOWS this file is built and not run; `program/test_guarded_region_examples_on_every_host` builds both arms for pe64 on every host and reads the scope tables, and `mir/test_seh_filter_with_a_branch` pins the funclet's shape.
